Akashti.name: Akashti
Akashti.publicNotes:
Akashtis are manipulative fiends who prey on those in mourning; they assume the form of a recently deceased loved one so they can infiltrate homes, then murder and consume the souls of grieving families. Sometimes called a "copycorpse," an akashti in its true form appears as a skin-covered skeleton with sharp talons on its fingers and tears of blood dripping from its lidless eyes. Its skull appears open like a bowl, and inside nest handfuls of crimson butterflies. When an akashti hides within its manifested body, close investigation can sometimes reveal the truth when the scalp of the supposed beloved one returned to life seems to subtly ripple and bulge as the butterflies within writhe. Akashtis embody the complex cycle of grief.

Deathly Invaders

Sometimes, akashtis ambush and murder objetivos not to bask in the grief of their loved ones, but instead to assume their form and infiltrate an organization from within to corrupt established bonds of camaraderie. Inevitably, though, these akashtis grow bored with DECEPTION and lead their new aliados into a trap for slaughter.

action->Soul Shred.name: Soul Shred
action->Soul Shred.description: Las criaturas killed by an akashti are difficult to bring back to life or animate as undead. The akashti automatically attempts to counteract any attempt to resurrect or animate as undead any criatura that it has killed (counteract modifier [[/r 1d20+19 #Counteract]]{+19}, counteract rank 5). If the akashti who slew the criatura is slain, the criatura can be brought back from death or become undead normally.

action->Manifest Body.name: Manifest Body
action->Manifest Body.description:
Frecuencia una vez al día

Efecto The akashti manifests a hollow humanoid body around its slender skeletal frame over the course of 10 minutos of concentration. If this time is spent within 10 pies of a humanoid body that has been dead for less than a week, the akashti's manifested body looks identical to that of the dead humanoid when they lived and functions as a disguise of that criatura. If the akashti can consume a portion of the body it's duplicating, it gains a +4 bonificador de circunstancia to DECEPTION checks to Impersonate the criatura. While wearing a manifested body, the akashti loses its claw Golpe, and its voice sounds like that of the dead criatura; it doesn't possess any of the dead criatura's memories or skills and must rely on DECEPTION to continue the charade in the face of scrutiny. An akashti's manifested body decays swiftly if it doesn't take 10 minutos una vez al día to maintain the manifestation of the false flesh. The body has 10 Puntos de golpe and the same defenses as the akashti. When the body is destroyed, the akashti emerges unharmed and the fleshy shell left behind scatters into a cloud of red butterflies that swiftly fade into red mist.

action->Stunning Despair.name: Stunning Despair
action->Stunning Despair.description: The akashti unleashes overwhelming sobs of despair. Las criaturas within 30 pies must attempt a @Check[will|dc:29] salvación or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Aturdido 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Aturdido 3} on a critical failure). The akashti can't use Stunning Despair again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Stunning Despair]]{1d4 asaltos}.

Algriever.name: Algriever
Algriever.publicNotes:
Some mistake these spiderlike spirits as scavengers looking to loot abandoned shrines, but they're actually the opposite: self-appointed guardians of forgotten places of worship, defending the sanctity of discarded faiths and tending sites that have no caretakers. Sometimes, an algriever's duties are tinged with sadness and grief, as they mourn the loss of those who once attended their chosen shrine. Others are filled with frustration and rage, viewing any who stumble upon their shrine as lapsed faithful at best or blasphemers at worse—sinners who deserve punishment.

Algrievers have little interest in living criaturas until they wander into their territory. Once an algriever's shrine has been breached, they block passage until the interlopers pay their respects. Aggressive algrievers steal from travelers or take hostages until their demands for an offering are satisfied. When algrievers suspect someone of committing blasphemy, no gifts can slake their thirst for vengeance.

Reactive Punishment

An algriever follows the edicts and anathemas of the deity or faith of the shrine to which they're bonded, although they remain neutral in alignment. Regardless of how large the shrine is, an algriever chooses three Medium or smaller objects in the shrine as their own focus for defense, and can use Acolyte's Defense against any criatura that touches or disturbs those objects.

Efecto The algriever Strides toward the criatura; this movement no desencadena reacciones. The algriever marks the criatura as its enemigo and gains a +2 bonificador de estado to tiradas de ataque against that enemigo until they select a new enemigo with Acolyte's Defense.

action->Shrine Bond.name: Shrine Bond
action->Shrine Bond.description: The algriever bonds with a shrine after they spend 24 horas at the site. While bonded, the algriever gains a +2 bonificador de circunstancia to Perception checks and pruebas de habilidad.

Argyrzei.name: Argyrzei
Argyrzei.publicNotes:
Most nindorus are harmed by silver, but not the argyrzei. Instead, argyrzeis use silver as a method of spreading sickness and pain, and to help them manipulate the minds of those who unwittingly fall under the curse of their infected gifts. They delight in disguising themselves and then selling or giving infected silver to victims. Other nindorus particularly fear argyrzeis for their mastery over silver, knowing that they're capable of causing painful wounds with their silver blades.

Argyrzeis appear humanoid, but their pies point backwards and they have no heads. Their glowing red neck stumps are stuffed with a wide assortment of knives, blades, and shards of metal. Estos nindorus represent the cycle of art being created, destroyed, and recycled into new art.

action->Cursesense.name: Cursesense
action->Cursesense.description: El argyrzei puede ver y oir a traves de cualquier objeto de plata que haya maldito, siempre que el objeto este a 1 milla o menos.

action->Headless.name: Headless
action->Headless.description: An argyrzei is headless but can still hear, speak, see, and smell as if it had a head. The argyrzei is immune to decapitation effects, such as those caused by vorpal armas.

action->Soul Shred.name: Soul Shred
action->Soul Shred.description: Las criaturas killed by an argyrzei are difficult to bring back to life or to animate as undead. The argyrzei automatically attempts to counteract any attempt to resurrect or animate as undead any criatura that it has killed (counteract modifier [[/r 1d20+23 #Counteract]]{+23}, counteract nivel 7th). If the argyrzei who slew the criatura is itself slain, the criatura can be brought back from death or become undead normally.

action->Infect Silver.name: Infect Silver
action->Infect Silver.description:
Frecuencia una vez al día

Efecto The argyrzei concentrates on an adjacent silver object that's no larger than Bulk 2. That object becomes cursed; if the object is being carried, the object's carrier can resist the object becoming cursed with a @Check[will|dc:33] salvación. The argyrzei can maintain up to five curses simultaneously; if it infects a sixth silver item, the oldest cursed item becomes uncursed.

RARE

CURSED

As long as tú remain cursed, sufres a –2 status penalties to all tiradas de salvación against mental effects created by nindorus.

Bakeneko.name: Bakeneko
Bakeneko.publicNotes:
A bakeneko comes into existence when the life of a cat is extended past its normal lifespan, whether through incredible fortune, magic, or other means. With each passing year, the feline becomes more and more monstrous—growing in size, becoming more intelligent, and gaining an affinity for magic. Eventually, they become able to walk upright on their rear legs, pursue new hobbies, and learn languages. Despite this expanded intellect, many bakenekos prefer to enjoy the first decades of their ascension continuing their lives as usual as a (particularly oversized) house cat. For some, they do so because they want to acquire knowledge of the world that they couldn't comprehend as cats, but for others, it's just a desire to live out their lives with their current families and loved ones before moving on to what comes next.

Bakenekos enjoy dancing above all other pleasures and can't resist nodding their heads, tapping their paws, or swishing their tails in time to music. They often animate corpses simply to watch them dance—a pastime that often conjuros trouble for nearby settlements should the undead get free from the bakeneko's control. Bakenekos typically have a playful and mischievous demeanor, and while they aren't inherently evil criaturas, they're still feared for their ability to animate corpses and command fire. Villagers are often asustado half to death by the sight of a flaming cat strolling alongside a walking corpse, and bakenekos' association with evil and the occult has caused some villages in Tian Xia to vilify all cats.

Nekomatas

Bakenekos mostly see their animated but mindless zombies as amusements, though they also use them as guardians or even as agents for revenge. Still, they do their best to ensure that undead they animate aren't left to wander free. Most tales of "evil bakenekos" in fact refer to a similar and much more dangerous criatura, the nekomata—a nivel 6 Medium-sized variant of the bakeneko whose bite causes a debilitating disease of the mind.

Guhdggi.name: Guhdggi
Guhdggi.publicNotes:
A guhdggi forms from the corrupted reincarnated souls of those who have trod the same pilgrimage route through multiple lives. Este type of nindoru looks like a bloated frog with long, slender human arms instead of front pies. Its eyes appear bulbous and blind yet are capable of sight. A guhdggi always carries a large wicker cage strapped to their back, while dozens of cords and straps affix a trove of broken armas, tools, and items to their belly and flanks. When they walk, they do so with the aid of two long spears clutched in their forearms, stumbling and hopping in an ungainly gait. The most unsettling feature of the guhdggi is its second face, revealed when the frog-like mouth opens to reveal a human face peering from its throat amid a tangled nest of butterflies. Este face has long, dark, animated hair capable of inflicting painful lashes, the lengths of which hang from the corner of the frog's mouth when its lips are closed.

While the guhdggi is no longer capable of movement as swift as most humanoids walk, they still enjoy traveling while harboring a ferocious jealousy of those who can do so with greater ease. One would do well not to underestimate the stumbling stagger of a guhdggi, though! The fiend particularly delights in lying in wait along isolated sections of pilgrimage routes to ambush travelers, trapping victims in their cages and feeding upon their captive's mind and memories of previously visited places.

Guhdggis embody the cycles of repeated journeys and the concept that every journey taken ends at the start of the next. Central to this concept is the notion that no journey ever truly begins or ends—they just emerge from the previous one.

When an evil mortal soul that has been reincarnated multiple times is wrenched from the cycle of souls and corrupted, it can undergo a horrific transformation into a fiend known as a nindoru. A force for entropy and the breaking of cycles, nindorus are hideous criaturas whose bodies often appear distorted, who wield armas that have been shattered yet still function, and whose true face is often escondido from view. They display rasgos one might expect to see in an undead criatura, such as decaying flesh or exposed bones, yet a nindoru is very much still alive.

Each nindoru epitomizes the fracture of a specific cycle, be it one from the natural world or from societal traditions. To the nindoru, nothing is more delicious than the consumption of a criatura who has reincarnated multiple times, with those who are theoretically about to ascend to true enlightenment presenting the tastiest meal. Those slain by a nindoru are themselves torn from the cycle—the lucky ones move on to the Boneyard for judgment, but many are instead corrupted to form more of these horrific fiends.

Followers of Sangpotshi find nindoru to be particularly abhorrent and count them among the greatest threats imaginable. Most commonly found in regions of the world where the reincarnation cycle is strongest, nindorus are, like rakshasas and oni, associated most strongly with the Material Plane.

Reincarnated Souls

In some cases, tú'll know if a criatura a nindoru attacks has a reincarnated soul. Ancestries like samsarans are always reincarnated souls, and a PC's backstory or even their background can often indicate the presence of a previous life. All of the PCs in Season of Ghosts qualify as reincarnated souls, as they've relived their lives over and over for decades. If tú ever need to determine if a criatura's soul is reincarnated for the purpose of adjudicating a nindoru's ability, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:11]—on a success, it has a reincarnated soul.

Nindoru Demigods

The most powerful nindorus are demigods, although their cults are quite rare. Prone to reincarnation after death, nindoru demigods like Kugaptee are more properly known as "nindoru ascetics."

Nindoru Traitors

While most nindorus are purely chaotic evil in NATURE, legends tell of exceptionally rare nindorus who manage to escape their own NATURE and ascend, reincarnating after death into kami or other more benevolent spirits and shedding the nindoru rasgo as they do so. Of course, these "traitors" are regarded as the most delicious meals imaginable by the nindorus left behind.

Nindoru Butterflies

One of the strangest shared rasgos of the various types of nindoru are the blood-red butterflies that seem to follow them around, nest on their bodies, or periodically emerge from their wounds. Estos unnerving insects are physical manifestations of the nindorus' thoughts and symbolize the countless past lives they once lived but turned their backs on. Nindoru butterflies never last long once they flutter more than a few pies from their source, fading away into smoke that quickly dissipates into the air.

Other Nindorus

Many other types of nindorus exist beyond the four presented on these pages. Others include the corpse-copying akashtis (sobbing nindorus), infiltrators of SOCIETY known as kagekumas (lurking nindorus), the dead defiling shisagishins (crooked nindorus), and the powerful and brutal argyrzeis (headless nindorus).

action->Cage Prey.description:
Requisitos The guhdggi has grappled a Medium or smaller criatura with its hair lash and doesn't have a criatura caged

Efecto The guhdggi attempts an @Check[athletics|against:reflex] prueba opposed by the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} criatura's CD de Reflejos. If it succeeds, it places the criatura into the cage it carries on its back. The guhdggi's hair lash no longer grapples the criatura, and it can't attack a criatura in its cage.

The caged criatura is grabbed. It takes @Damage[(2d4+6)[mental]] daño when first caged and at the end of each of its turns while it's caged. A caged victim can attempt to [[/act force-open dc=22]] or [[/act escape dc=22]] the cage with a DC 22 prueba, or it can attack the cage's wicker bars, but only with ataques sin armas or with armas of light Bulk or less. Other criaturas can attack the wicker bars as well but can't attempt to FORCE OPEN the cage or aid a caged criatura's Escape if the guhdggi can resist. Attacks against the cage resolve against the guhdggi's AC, and if the cage takes at least 16 bludgeoning or daño cortante from a single attack or conjuro, the caged criatura gets free.

If the guhdggi dies, its cage crumbles to fragments.

action->Lurching Skewer.name: Lurching Skewer
action->Lurching Skewer.description: The guhdggi Strides, then makes two spear Golpes, one with each of the two spears it wields. Both Golpes must have the same objetivo. Apply the guhdggi's multiple attack penalizador to each Golpe normally.

action->Manifest Tool.name: Manifest Tool
action->Manifest Tool.description:
Frecuencia una vez por hora

Efecto The guhdggi manifests a tool from its thoughts. If its next action is to attempt a prueba de habilidad that could be affected by the tool it chose, it gains a +2 bonificador por objeto to the prueba de habilidad. The tool is then destroyed.

action->Ruin Wielder.name: Ruin Wielder
action->Ruin Wielder.description: When a guhdggi wields a broken non-magical arma, they do not take any of the disadvantages of the arma being broken. While the guhdggi wields it, the arma becomes a +1 striking arma that deals an additional 1d6 daño mental on a successful hit.

Ijda.name: Ijda
Ijda.publicNotes:
Ijdas are criaturas of forgetfulness. Born from souls who were once enlightened but then renounced it and their role in the cycle of reincarnation, they curse the futility of their existence and find pleasure in leading others to the same fate.

Ijdas appear as towering humanoids, their bodies bloated and constantly bursting with small red butterflies that flitter away before melting into mist. Their arms are overly long and so broken as to writhe more like tentacles, affording them an unsettling combat style with greater reach than most large criaturas enjoy. They wear clothing and capes made of moldy straw and wield broken swords whose shattered blades still float roughly in place. Their most unsettling features are their complete lack of heads; instead, where a head should be sits a wicker cage filled with a writhing cloud of butterflies. Yet still, they see, hear, and speak without issue, as if their heads remained in place.

Formed without heads or even brains, an idja's mind is shared among the flocks of butterflies in their head cages or bursting from their bodies, and as each of these insects escapes and fades away, these forgetful fiends lose another potential thought. Unable to learn new things, any actions they take stem from memories etched into their souls or directives they blindly follow from other nindorus or criaturas they've come to accept as superiors. Their movements, words, and reactions are all conducted via a type of muscle memory based on how their souls believe they should respond to their external stimuli. As a result, most now serve as brutal guardians, since their forgetfulness also prevents them from being able to sleep.

Kagekuma.name: Kagekuma
Kagekuma.publicNotes:
Kagekumas exist in the periphery, lurking in the very shadows of their prey. Known in some regions as "shadefiends," this nindoru's ability to appear as uninteresting figures in the crowd allows them to feed even in populated areas. A kagekuma appears as a hunched over humanoid with a long neck and a fanged mouth, but when wearing a bundle, the criatura's head and neck tuck in tight between its shoulders to become entirely obscured. The kagekuma personifies the cycle of trust being built and broken over and over again through the course of a complex relationship.

Kagekuma Bundles

A kagekuma's bundle is more than just a disguise and armadura—it's a physical indication of how many lives they've cut short and how many souls they've supped upon. Whether the bundle is composed of straw, ropes, hair, or other materials, the individual lengths symbolize a sort of "reaper's harvest," with each strand in the bundle representing a metaphorical lifeline that the nindoru has severed and collected—to an extent that the multitude of lives taken overwhelms the nindoru's own presence in the world.

Meokdan.name: Meokdan
Meokdan.publicNotes:
As the least of their kind, meokdans suffer a constant and painful hunger, for they lack the ability of more powerful nindorus to derive nourishment from a reincarnated soul. Este hunger drives the meokdan to constantly seek food and often compels them to eat dirt, stones, and refuse that offer little (if any) nutritional value. Regardless of how much they eat, a meokdan always remains painfully thin in stature. Regardless of how hungry they get, they never starve to death.

A meokdan's emaciated frame appears human in shape, with thick, tangled hair that grows directly from their face as well as the rest of their head, leaving only the meokdan's gaping mouth visible. Their arms appear to be broken and unnaturally long, with equally long fingers tipped with ragged nails. Small, open sores pockmark their skin.

Meokdans epitomize the cycle of food, from consumption to the criatura themselves being consumed in the end, be it by predators or the environment growing from their remains.

When an evil mortal soul that has been reincarnated multiple times is wrenched from the cycle of souls and corrupted, it can undergo a horrific transformation into a fiend known as a nindoru. A force for entropy and the breaking of cycles, nindorus are hideous criaturas whose bodies often appear distorted, who wield armas that have been shattered yet still function, and whose true face is often escondido from view. They display rasgos one might expect to see in an undead criatura, such as decaying flesh or exposed bones, yet a nindoru is very much still alive.

Each nindoru epitomizes the fracture of a specific cycle, be it one from the natural world or from societal traditions. To the nindoru, nothing is more delicious than the consumption of a criatura who has reincarnated multiple times, with those who are theoretically about to ascend to true enlightenment presenting the tastiest meal. Those slain by a nindoru are themselves torn from the cycle—the lucky ones move on to the Boneyard for judgment, but many are instead corrupted to form more of these horrific fiends.

Followers of Sangpotshi find nindoru to be particularly abhorrent and count them among the greatest threats imaginable. Most commonly found in regions of the world where the reincarnation cycle is strongest, nindorus are, like rakshasas and oni, associated most strongly with the Material Plane.

Reincarnated Souls

In some cases, tú'll know if a criatura a nindoru attacks has a reincarnated soul. Ancestries like samsarans are always reincarnated souls, and a PC's backstory or even their background can often indicate the presence of a previous life. All of the PCs in Season of Ghosts qualify as reincarnated souls, as they've relived their lives over and over for decades. If tú ever need to determine if a criatura's soul is reincarnated for the purpose of adjudicating a nindoru's ability, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:11]—on a success, it has a reincarnated soul.

Nindoru Demigods

The most powerful nindorus are demigods, although their cults are quite rare. Prone to reincarnation after death, nindoru demigods like Kugaptee are more properly known as "nindoru ascetics."

Nindoru Traitors

While most nindorus are purely chaotic evil in NATURE, legends tell of exceptionally rare nindorus who manage to escape their own NATURE and ascend, reincarnating after death into kami or other more benevolent spirits and shedding the nindoru rasgo as they do so. Of course, these "traitors" are regarded as the most delicious meals imaginable by the nindorus left behind.

Nindoru Butterflies

One of the strangest shared rasgos of the various types of nindoru are the blood-red butterflies that seem to follow them around, nest on their bodies, or periodically emerge from their wounds. Estos unnerving insects are physical manifestations of the nindorus' thoughts and symbolize the countless past lives they once lived but turned their backs on. Nindoru butterflies never last long once they flutter more than a few pies from their source, fading away into smoke that quickly dissipates into the air.

Other Nindorus

Many other types of nindorus exist beyond the four presented on these pages. Others include the corpse-copying akashtis (sobbing nindorus), infiltrators of SOCIETY known as kagekumas (lurking nindorus), the dead defiling shisagishins (crooked nindorus), and the powerful and brutal argyrzeis (headless nindorus).

Noppera-bo Grunt.name: Soldado noppera-bo
Noppera-bo Grunt.publicNotes:
Los soldados noppera-bo carecen de la soltura social necesaria para disfrazarse por completo con el rostro de otra persona.

Los noppera-bo parecen humanos normales vistos desde atrás, e incluso podrían parecerse a alguien que conoces, hasta que se vuelven y revelan un rostro sin facciones.

Profesionales consumados

Aunque el noppera-bo típico es cruel y disfruta asustando o atormentando a criaturas humanoides, no todos se recrean en la maldad. Los noppera-bo neutrales suelen ser bromistas que usan sus aptitudes para engañar y tomar el pelo, mientras que los raros noppera-bo buenos usan sus dones para honrar e idealizar a quienes admiran, dedicando su propio tiempo a desarrollar sus habilidades artísticas o de artesanía.

Orígenes de los noppera-bo

Existen muchas teorías sobre el origen de los noppera-bo: desde tanukis cuya aptitud de cambiar de forma salió mal, hasta humanoides deformados por maldiciones o yokai surgidos de forma natural. Algunos incluso teorizan que esta condición es una maldición transmisible, como la licantropía. La mayoría de los noppera-bo no recuerdan sus orígenes y suelen estar más interesados en fingir ser otra persona por completo.

Red-Hooded Thatchling.publicNotes:
Cuando un alma condenada a convertirse en thatchling muere entre grandes angustias, puede regresar tras la muerte como un thatchling de capucha roja. Estos thatchlings vengativos parecen llevar capuchas rojas vistos desde lejos, pero de cerca se revela la verdad macabra: sus cabezas están empapadas de sangre. A diferencia de otros thatchlings, los thatchlings de capucha roja son hábiles con el engaño, y su capacidad para parecer humanoides vivos mediante magia de ilusión les permite atraer a los desprevenidos a emboscadas con mucha más facilidad.

En el Shenmen rural, algunas ramas del Sangpotshi advierten de lo que puede suceder si a un alma destinada a reencarnarse se le impide entrar en el Río de las Almas y reincorporarse al ciclo. Estas almas se frustran, se confunden y luego se enfurecen por lo que sienten como la negación del cuerpo que merecen; a cambio, obligan a la vegetación a servirles como nuevo cuerpo. Otros teorizan que, cuando un cadáver se entierra en una tumba poco profunda, las raíces de la hierba que crecen hacia los restos pueden enredar el alma y atraparla.

Los thatchlings son inteligentes y capaces de hablar, pero rara vez lo hacen; por lo general tienen poco que decir a quienes poseen las vidas que codician. En raras ocasiones, uno podría intentar atraer a alguien hacia una zona de hierba alta o maleza densa pidiendo ayuda a gritos, pero tienen poca habilidad para el Engaño, por lo que estas tácticas no resultan especialmente eficaces para hacerlos pasar por criaturas vivas necesitadas de auxilio.

Viejos amigos

El origen de los thatchlings de Willowshore es el simple hecho de que las almas que normalmente se habrían reencarnado tras morir no pueden hacerlo, y por eso se alzan como thatchlings. Por supuesto, como cada año "se reinicia", quienes murieron durante el año y se convirtieron en thatchlings renacen con vida una vez más el primer día del verano, sin recuerdos de su existencia anterior condenada. Aunque siguen impulsados por el instinto de atacar a los vivos, los thatchlings de Willowshore sienten cierto remordimiento; si el DJ lo considera especialmente apropiado, podrían sufrir un penalizador de circunstancia -2 a las tiradas de ataque y tiradas de salvación contra criaturas a las que conocieron en vida.

Siempre desorientados

La maldición del thatchling roba el sentido de la orientación a quienes caen bajo ella, lo que ha dado lugar a toda una categoría de insultos en Shenmen que comparan la capacidad de alguien para hacer algo con "el sentido de un thatchling". Por ejemplo, de alguien a quien le cuesta hacer amigos podría decirse que tiene "el sentido de amistad de un thatchling", mientras que de alguien que arruina comidas constantemente podría decirse que tiene "el sentido culinario de un thatchling".

Handmade Habitats

Un shisagishin prefers a roam areas already rife con conflict y potential accidents, but ello va a happily create such un location si needed. They might veneno wells, introduce disease a healthy livestock, o even collaborate con corrupt humans si ello means el freedom a kill. Cursed towns o haunted roads son sometimes el playground de such un shisagishin.

action->Soul Shred.name: Soul Shred

When a home is abandoned after it has been lived in for generations, sometimes the building itself mourns the loss of its family so greatly that it attracts the pity of a kami who has yet to claim a ward. Similar to how a tsukumogami manifests, such a conjoining of spiritual power can result in the formation of a silsyche—a spirit of an abandoned home who craves companionship. A silsyche never aims to outright harm those who enter the homes they form from. They are merely desperate for connection and lack the understanding that most others don't take kindly to captivity.

The silsyche's true form is a slender, childlike shimmering figure with a headpiece resembling the structure they initially manifested from. Estos representations of the silsyche's first home reflect the warmth and welcome they yearn for, potentially even displaying mementos of the house's inhabitants that have long gone.

Range Of Possession

Most silsyches bond with a single home, typically a small building with one or two floors. More powerful silsyches can bond with larger structures, like fortresses or castles, or even large vehicles like sailing ships. Legends of entire towns being claimed by a single, incredibly powerful silsyche persist in stories to this day.

action->Inhabit Home.name: Inhabit Home
action->Inhabit Home.description: The silsyche inhabits a modest building and controls it. While the building is possessed, its decor shifts to reflect the silsyche's mood, such as being filled with bright light (when the silsyche is happy) or appearing old and filthy (if they're depressed). A silsyche can't willingly leave their home; if forced out of their home, the silsyche takes @Damage[3d10[force]] daño (@Check[fortitude|dc:25|basic] salvación) at the start of each of their turns.

action->Rejuvenation.name: Rejuvenecimiento

Fallo crítico As failure, but the criatura becomes hostile to anyone who tries to make them leave the building. The criatura can only attempt another salvación de Voluntad to end the effect at the end of any turn in which they attack an aliado.

Sojiruh.name: Sojiruh
Sojiruh.publicNotes:
A sojiruh comes into existence when a criatura who has dedicated multiple lives to achieving enlightenment turns their back on these goals and deliberately tears themselves away from the cycle of reincarnation before their death. Estos monstrous criaturas are the most common nindoru and are also the most hated by followers of Sangpotshi, since so many of these fiends rise from fallen members of that very philosophy.

Este type of nindoru relishes the flavor of an oft-reincarnated soul and finds this life force tastes best when consumed while the physical body still lives and screams. To sojiruhs, the sound of a perfect scream from the body it feeds upon is akin to the perfect wine pairing with dinner.

A sojiruh's mouth is stitched shut with lengths of its own hair. Despite this, they can speak freely, their hollow-sounding voices issuing clearly from sealed lips. They only stretch these stitches when they elige to shriek and scream. Their arms are long and broken-looking, while their chests are little more than rib cages filled with red wet butterflies that crawl through and cling to the criatura's ribs and organs. When a sojiruh screams, the wings of the butterflies in its chest flutter frantically.

Sojiruhs symbolize the cycle of reincarnation come undone from its purity and becoming mired in decay and corruption.

When an evil mortal soul that has been reincarnated multiple times is wrenched from the cycle of souls and corrupted, it can undergo a horrific transformation into a fiend known as a nindoru. A force for entropy and the breaking of cycles, nindorus are hideous criaturas whose bodies often appear distorted, who wield armas that have been shattered yet still function, and whose true face is often escondido from view. They display rasgos one might expect to see in an undead criatura, such as decaying flesh or exposed bones, yet a nindoru is very much still alive.

Each nindoru epitomizes the fracture of a specific cycle, be it one from the natural world or from societal traditions. To the nindoru, nothing is more delicious than the consumption of a criatura who has reincarnated multiple times, with those who are theoretically about to ascend to true enlightenment presenting the tastiest meal. Those slain by a nindoru are themselves torn from the cycle—the lucky ones move on to the Boneyard for judgment, but many are instead corrupted to form more of these horrific fiends.

Followers of Sangpotshi find nindoru to be particularly abhorrent and count them among the greatest threats imaginable. Most commonly found in regions of the world where the reincarnation cycle is strongest, nindorus are, like rakshasas and oni, associated most strongly with the Material Plane.

Reincarnated Souls

In some cases, tú'll know if a criatura a nindoru attacks has a reincarnated soul. Ancestries like samsarans are always reincarnated souls, and a PC's backstory or even their background can often indicate the presence of a previous life. All of the PCs in Season of Ghosts qualify as reincarnated souls, as they've relived their lives over and over for decades. If tú ever need to determine if a criatura's soul is reincarnated for the purpose of adjudicating a nindoru's ability, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:11]—on a success, it has a reincarnated soul.

Nindoru Demigods

The most powerful nindorus are demigods, although their cults are quite rare. Prone to reincarnation after death, nindoru demigods like Kugaptee are more properly known as "nindoru ascetics."

Nindoru Traitors

While most nindorus are purely chaotic evil in NATURE, legends tell of exceptionally rare nindorus who manage to escape their own NATURE and ascend, reincarnating after death into kami or other more benevolent spirits and shedding the nindoru rasgo as they do so. Of course, these "traitors" are regarded as the most delicious meals imaginable by the nindorus left behind.

Nindoru Butterflies

One of the strangest shared rasgos of the various types of nindoru are the blood-red butterflies that seem to follow them around, nest on their bodies, or periodically emerge from their wounds. Estos unnerving insects are physical manifestations of the nindorus' thoughts and symbolize the countless past lives they once lived but turned their backs on. Nindoru butterflies never last long once they flutter more than a few pies from their source, fading away into smoke that quickly dissipates into the air.

Other Nindorus

Many other types of nindorus exist beyond the four presented on these pages. Others include the corpse-copying akashtis (sobbing nindorus), infiltrators of SOCIETY known as kagekumas (lurking nindorus), the dead defiling shisagishins (crooked nindorus), and the powerful and brutal argyrzeis (headless nindorus).

Thatchling.name: Thatchling
Thatchling.publicNotes:
El thatchling típico parece un fardo humanoide de hierba seca y ramitas, unido por mechones de lo que parece cabello azul brillante. Estos muertos vivientes menores no pueden formar cuerpos más grandes que los de un niño humano pequeño.

En el Shenmen rural, algunas ramas del Sangpotshi advierten de lo que puede suceder si a un alma destinada a reencarnarse se le impide entrar en el Río de las Almas y reincorporarse al ciclo. Estas almas se frustran, se confunden y luego se enfurecen por lo que sienten como la negación del cuerpo que merecen; a cambio, obligan a la vegetación a servirles como nuevo cuerpo. Otros teorizan que, cuando un cadáver se entierra en una tumba poco profunda, las raíces de la hierba que crecen hacia los restos pueden enredar el alma y atraparla.

Los thatchlings son inteligentes y capaces de hablar, pero rara vez lo hacen; por lo general tienen poco que decir a quienes poseen las vidas que codician. En raras ocasiones, uno podría intentar atraer a alguien hacia una zona de hierba alta o maleza densa pidiendo ayuda a gritos, pero tienen poca habilidad para el Engaño, por lo que estas tácticas no resultan especialmente eficaces para hacerlos pasar por criaturas vivas necesitadas de auxilio.

Viejos amigos

El origen de los thatchlings de Willowshore es el simple hecho de que las almas que normalmente se habrían reencarnado tras morir no pueden hacerlo, y por eso se alzan como thatchlings. Por supuesto, como cada año "se reinicia", quienes murieron durante el año y se convirtieron en thatchlings renacen con vida una vez más el primer día del verano, sin recuerdos de su existencia anterior condenada. Aunque siguen impulsados por el instinto de atacar a los vivos, los thatchlings de Willowshore sienten cierto remordimiento; si el DJ lo considera especialmente apropiado, podrían sufrir un penalizador de circunstancia -2 a las tiradas de ataque y tiradas de salvación contra criaturas a las que conocieron en vida.

Siempre desorientados

La maldición del thatchling roba el sentido de la orientación a quienes caen bajo ella, lo que ha dado lugar a toda una categoría de insultos en Shenmen que comparan la capacidad de alguien para hacer algo con "el sentido de un thatchling". Por ejemplo, de alguien a quien le cuesta hacer amigos podría decirse que tiene "el sentido de amistad de un thatchling", mientras que de alguien que arruina comidas constantemente podría decirse que tiene "el sentido culinario de un thatchling".

action->Distracting Giggle.name: Distracting Giggle
action->Distracting Giggle.description: 15 pies. The thatchling's giggle echoes in the back of the mind. Las criaturas within the aura take a –1 penalizador de estado to Will saves.

A thatchling is always permanently destroyed if reduced to 0 Puntos de golpe by daño de fuego or if the obstacle preventing the soul from reincarnating is removed.

action->Thatchling's Curse.description:

Éxito crítico El objetivo is unaffected and is temporarily immune to Thatchling's Curse for 24 horas.

In addition, when the cursed criatura attempts a SURVIVAL prueba to Sense Direction or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EA5vuSgJfiHH7plD]{Track}, they use the outcome for one degree of success worse than the result of their prueba, and they can't take the Scout exploration activity.

action->Thicket Walker.description: Thatchlings ignore difficult terrain caused by brambles, tangled grass, and undergrowth, even those manipulated by magic.
